interest: This document illustrates the administrative indexing and cross-referencing practices of the U.S. State Department's central decimal filing system, showing how etiquette and protocol questions arising at overseas missions were cross-indexed between bilateral country files (894.452) and domestic etiquette files (811.452/156). Substantively, it highlights the delicate protocol challenges faced by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo concerning the relative precedence of foreign ministers plenipotentiary versus the Under Secretary of State and visiting or retired American diplomats at diplomatic functions.
overview: This file consists of a single-page State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet for decimal file 894.452 (Precedence - Japan). It indexes Telegram No. 65 dated March 3 from U.S. Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Japan, who inquired about prevailing Washington protocol regarding the relative precedence between foreign ministers plenipotentiary, the Under Secretary of State, and American ambassadors and ministers on leave or in retirement. The notation indicates that the underlying telegram was cross-referenced and filed under decimal classification 811.452/156.

subfiles.about: A State Department List of Papers sheet recording an inquiry by Ambassador Grew regarding diplomatic precedence.
subfiles.summary: This List of Papers sheet for decimal file 894.452 records Telegram No. 65 sent on March 3 by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew from Japan. The entry summarizes Grew's inquiry into the Washington rules of precedence for foreign ministers plenipotentiary in relation to the Under Secretary of State and American ambassadors or ministers who are retired or on leave. The sheet directs researchers to the main document filed under 811.452/156.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Precedence - Japan (Telegram No. 65 from Grew)
